Seminar Title:

Aspects of optimal quantization for nonuniform densities on spherical curves

Seminar Type:

Sangita Jha

Abstract: 

In this report, the optimal quantization of probability measures with nonuniform densities on spherical curves is investigated. 
While classical quantization theory has primarily focused on uniform probability distributions,many real-world data sets exhibit significant nonuniformity. 
To address this gap, the centroid condition for optimal quantizers is derived, followed by a high-resolution asymptotic analysis
 to establish the corresponding point-density formula. The asymptotic error formula for nonuniform probability densities is also derived. 
The theoretical results are applied to von Mises distributions, and the corresponding optimal quantization 
conditions are characterized. Applications of the high-resolution asymptotic formula and its associated error formula are further presented,
 including a comparison between geodesic and chordal distortions. The Lloyd map is used for graphical representation and analysis of the optimal quantizers.
 Furthermore, the developed framework is applied to cosine-modulated densities, and symmetric quantizers are studied in connection with the Lloyd map. 
These results provide a foundation for further developments in geometric probability theory, quantization theory on spherical curves, 
directional statistics, and modern engineering applications.
